questions.question: A force {F}=(2 {i}+3 {j}+2 {k}) N acts on a particle of mass m . The particle starts from point A(1,2,1) and moves to point B(3,4,3) . What is the total work done by the force on the particle?
questions.explanation: Work done by a constant force F⃗{F} is given by the dot product F⃗⋅d⃗{F}{d}, where d⃗{d} is the displacement from the initial point AA to the final point BB. Displacement d⃗{d}: d⃗=(xB−xA)i^  +  (yB−yA)j^  +  (zB−zA)k^=(3−1)i^+(4−2)j^+(3−1)k^=2i^+2j^+2k^.{d} = (x_B - x_A){i} \;+\; (y_B - y_A){j} \;+\; (z_B - z_A){k} = (3-1){i} + (4-2){j} + (3-1){k} = 2{i} + 2{j} + 2{k}. Dot product with F⃗=2i^+3j^+2k(F) = 2{i} + 3{j} + 2{k}: W=F⃗⋅d⃗=(2)(2)+(3)(2)+(2)(2)=4+6+4=14 J.W = {F}{d} = (2)(2) + (3)(2) + (2)(2) = 4 + 6 + 4 = 14\,{J}. Hence, the total work done on the particle is 14 J.

questions.question: A sphere of mass m is tied to end of a string of length l and rotated through the other end along a horizontal circular path with speed v . The work done by centripetal force in full horizontal circle is:
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal force always acts radially inward, perpendicular to the tangential displacement of the mass. Hence, the dot product of force and displacement is zero at each instant, and the total work done over one full revolution is W  =  ∫F⃗centripetal⋅dr⃗  =  0.W \;=\; {F}_{{centripetal}} d{r} \;=\;0.

questions.question: A body of mass m is moving in a circle of radius r with a constant speed v . The force on the body is {m v²}{r} and it is directed towards the centre. What is the work done by this force in moving the body over half the circumference of the circle?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal force acts radially inward while the displacement is tangential at every point. Since the force is perpendicular to the displacement at all times, its dot product with displacement is zero at each instant. Hence, the net work done over half (or any portion) of the circle is 0.

questions.question: If a person is pushing a box inside a moving train, the work done in the frame of earth will be: {S}= displacement of the train relative to ground. {S}_{0}= displacement of the box w.r.t. train.
questions.explanation: Viewed from the ground (earth) frame, the actual displacement of the box is the vector sum of: S⃗{S}, the displacement of the train relative to the ground, and S⃗0{S}_0, the displacement of the box relative to the train. Hence, in the ground frame, the work done by the force F⃗{F} on the box is Wearth  =  F⃗ ⋅ (S⃗+S⃗0).W_{{earth}} \;=\;{F}\,\,({S} + {S}_0).

questions.question: A weightlifter lifts a weight off the ground and holds it up, then
options: Work is done in lifting as well as holding the weight
No work is done in both lifting and holding the weight
Work is done in lifting the weight but no work is required to be done in holding it up
No work is done in lifting the weight but work is required to be done in holding it up
questions.explanation: When lifting the weight, the weightlifter applies a force over a displacement, doing work against gravity. However, while holding the weight still, there is no displacement, so no work is done according to the definition W=F⃗⋅d⃗W = {F} {d}.

questions.question: In case of negative work the angle between the force and displacement is
questions.explanation: For work W=Fdcos⁡θW = Fd to be negative, the cosine term must be negative. This occurs when θ=180∘ = 180^ (i.e., the force and displacement are in opposite directions).

questions.question: If the angle between force and displacement is......... then work done is said to be zero.
questions.explanation: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement, the work done is given by W=F d cos⁡θ.W = F\,d\,. Since cos⁡90∘=0 90^ = 0, the work done is zero.

questions.question: A person of mass {m} is standing on one end of a plank of mass M and length L and floating in water. The person moves from one end to another and stops. Work done by normal force is -
questions.explanation: Since the person’s motion is purely horizontal along the plank (which stays afloat and horizontal), the normal force acts vertically. Therefore, the displacement and the normal force are perpendicular throughout. Hence, their dot product is zero and the work done by the normal force is W  =  N⃗ ⋅ d⃗  =  0.W \;=\;{N}\,\,{d}\;=\;0.

questions.question: If a body of mass 2 {~kg} is moved in the conservative field from point A to B in three different paths, then work done will be
questions.explanation: In a conservative field, the work done in moving a body between two fixed points depends only on those points, not on the path taken. Therefore, all three paths from AA to BB yield the same work.

questions.question: A body of mass 1 {~kg} is thrown upwards with a velocity 20 {~ms}^{-1} . It momentarily comes to rest after attaining a height of 18 {~m} . How much energy is lost due to air friction? (g=10 {~ms}^{-2})
questions.explanation: Initial Kinetic Energy: Ki=12 m v²=12×1×(20)2=200 J.K_i = 12\,m\,v² = 12 1 (20)² = 200\,{J}. Final Gravitational Potential Energy:The body rises to 18 m and comes to rest: Uf=m g h=1×10×18=180 J.U_f = m\,g\,h = 11018 = 180\,{J}. Energy Loss to Air Friction: ΔE=Ki−Uf=200−180=20 J. E = K_i - U_f = 200 - 180 = 20\,{J}. Thus, 20 J of energy is lost to air friction.

Work–Energy Theorem:Let WgW_g be the work by gravity (− mgh-\,mgh) and WfricW_{{fric}} be the frictional work. Then Wg+Wfric=ΔK=0−12 m v².W_g + W_{{fric}} = K = 0 - 12\,m\,v². questions.question: A block of mass √(2) {~kg} is released from the top of an inclined smooth surface as shown in figure. If spring constant of spring is 100 {~N} / {m} and block comes to rest after compressing the spring by 1 {~m} , then the distance travelled by block before it comes to rest is
questions.explanation: Along the Incline: Block mass: m=2 kgm = √(2)\,{kg} Incline angle: 45∘45^   ⟹  sin⁡45∘=12 45^=1/√2 Gravitational force component along the plane: mgsin⁡45∘=(2)(10)(12)=10 N.mg45^ = (√(2))(10)(1/√2)=10\,{N}. Spring Energy: Spring constant: k=100 N/mk = 100\,{N/m} Maximum compression: x=1 mx = 1\,{m} Energy stored in the spring: U=12kx²=12(100)(1)2=50 J.U = {1}{2}kx² = 1/2(100)(1)²=50\,{J}. Energy Conservation: The gravitational work done along the plane, W=10 SW = 10\,S, must equal the spring energy (50 J50\,{J}): 10 S=50⟹S=5 m.10 \, S = 50 S=5\,{m}. Thus, the block travels 5 m along the incline before coming to rest.

questions.question: A block of mass m initially at rest is dropped from a height h on to a spring of force constant k . The maximum compression in the spring is x then
questions.explanation: Just before touching the spring, the block has descended through height hh, converting its potential energy mghmgh into kinetic. It then compresses the spring by an additional distance xx, during which it loses a further potential energy mg xmg\,x. At maximum compression, the block’s speed is zero. Hence all of its lost gravitational potential energy, mg(h+x)mg(h + x), becomes spring potential energy 12 k x²12\,k\,x². Thus,mg (h+x)  =  12 k x².{mg\,(h+x)\;=\;12\,k\,x².}

hi.question: प्रारंभ में विरामावस्था पर स्थित द्रव्यमान m के एक गुटका को ऊँचाई h से बल नियतांक k की एक स्प्रिंग पर गिराया जाता है। स्प्रिंग में अधिकतम संपीडन x है, तो:
hi.explanation: स्प्रिंग को छूने से ठीक पहले, ब्लॉक h ऊँचाई तक नीचे आ चुका होता है, जिससे उसकी स्थितिज ऊर्जा mgh गतिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित हो जाती है। इसके बाद वह स्प्रिंग को अतिरिक्त दूरी x तक संपीड़ित (compress) करता है, जिसके दौरान वह mgx और स्थितिज ऊर्जा खो देता है। अधिकतम संपीड़न (maximum compression) पर ब्लॉक का वेग शून्य हो जाता है। अतः उसकी खोई हुई कुल गुरुत्वीय स्थितिज ऊर्जा mg(h+x), स्प्रिंग की स्थितिज ऊर्जा 12 k x²12\,k\,x²में परिवर्तित हो जाती है। अतः, ,mg (h+x)  =  12 k x².{mg\,(h+x)\;=\;12\,k\,x².}

questions.question: If we throw a body upwards with velocity of 4 {m} / {s} , at what height does its kinetic energy reduce to half of the initial value? (Take g=10 {~m} {~s}^{-2} )
questions.explanation: Initial Kinetic Energy: Ki=12 m v²=12 m (42)=8 m.K_i = 12\,m\,v² = 12 \,m\,(4²)=8\,m. When KK is half of its initial value: Knew=12 Ki=4 m.K_{{new}}=12\,K_i=4\,m. Potential Energy Gained (ΔU U):Since total mechanical energy EE remains constant and equals 8 m8\,m: Unew=E−Knew=8 m−4 m=4 m.U_{{new}}= E - K_{{new}}= 8\,m -4\,m=4\,m. Relate UnewU_{{new}} to Height hh: Unew=m g h=4 m    ⟹    h=4 mm g=410=0.4 m.U_{{new}}=m\,g\,h =4\,m \;\;\;\; h=4\,m/m\,g =4/10 =0.4\,{m}. Hence, the height at which the kinetic energy is half its initial value is 0.4 m.

questions.question: Initially mass m is held such that spring is in relaxed condition. If mass m is suddenly released, maximum elongation in spring will be
questions.explanation: Energy Conservation at Maximum Extension:At maximum extension XX, the block momentarily stops, so its kinetic energy is 0. The loss in gravitational potential energy equals the gain in spring potential energy: 12kX²=mgX.1/2kX² = mgX. Solve for XX:Divide both sides by XX (discarding the trivial solution X=0X=0): 12kX=mg⟹X=2mgk.1/2kX = mg X = 2mg/k. Thus, the maximum extension is 2mgk2mg/k.

A particle is moving in a circular path of radius a under the action of an attractive potential U =-k2r². Its total energy is:
questions.explanation: Given: Attractive potential: U=−k2a²U = -k/2a² Circular motion with radius aa. Step 1: Force from Potential Energy The force is F=−dUda=ka³F = -dU/da = k/a³. Step 2: Centripetal Force Centripetal force is F=mv²aF = mv²/a, equating it to the force from the potential: mv²a=ka³⇒v²=kma²mv²/a = k/a³ v² = k/ma² Step 3: Kinetic Energy The kinetic energy is: K=12mv²=k2a²K = 1/2mv² = k/2a² Step 4: Total Energy The total energy is: E=K+U=k2a²−k2a²=0E = K + U = k/2a² - k/2a² = 0

questions.question: Figure shows the vertical section of frictionless surface. A block of mass 2 {~kg} is released from the position {A} ; its {KE} as it reaches the position {C} is ({g}=10 {~m} / {s}²):-
questions.explanation: Since the track is frictionless and the block is released from rest at AA (height 14 m), all the gravitational potential energy lost from AA to CC (height 7 m) converts into kinetic energy: Height Drop =14−7=7= 14 - 7 = 7 m. Potential Energy Lost =m g Δh=2×10×7=140= m\,g\, h = 2 10 7 = 140 J. Hence, the kinetic energy of the block at CC is 140 J.

questions.question: A block of mass m is slowly made to move up the incline by a force F which is directed along the tangent of trajectory. is the coefficient of friction between the block and the incline.
options: A - R B - P C - S D - T
A - P B - R C - S D - T
A - R B -S C -P D - T
A - S B - P C - R D - T
questions.explanation: Work by gravity (A)The block’s center of mass rises through height hh. Hence Wgravity=− m g h    ⇒  (A)→(R).W_{gravity}=-\,m\,g\,h \;\;\; (A)(R). Work by friction (B)If the path length is ll, friction always opposes motion, so Wfriction=− μ m g l    ⇒  (B)→(P).W_{friction}=-\,\,m\,g\,l \;\;\; (B)(P). Work by applied force FF (C)The block moves “slowly” (ΔK=0 K=0), so FF must balance both gravity and friction. Thus WF=+ m g h  +  μ m g l    ⇒  (C)→(S).W_F = +\,m\,g\,h \;+\;\,m\,g\,l \;\;\; (C)(S). Total work on the block (D)Since the block’s kinetic energy does not change, the net work is zero: Wnet=0    ⇒  (D)→(T).W_{net}=0 \;\;\;(D)(T).

questions.question: If 250 {~J} of work is done in sliding a 5 {~kg} block up an inclined plane of height 4 {~m} . Work done against friction is: (g=10 {~ms}^{-2})
questions.explanation: Use energy accounting. The block gains gravitational potential energy mgh=(5)(10)(4)=200 Jmgh = (5)(10)(4)=200\,{J}. Since a total of 250 J of work was done in sliding the block up, the remainder Wfric=(Total work)−(Gain in potential energy)=250−200=50 JW_{{fric}} = {(Total work)} - {(Gain in potential energy)} = 250 - 200 = 50\,{J} must be the work done against friction.

questions.question: An open knife edge of mass m is dropped from a height h on a wooden floor. If the blade penetrates upto the depth d into the wood, the average resistance offered by the wood to the knife edge is
questions.explanation: Total Energy Lost:When the knife of mass mm is dropped from height hh and then penetrates the wood by distance dd, it loses potential energy: ΔU=mg (h+d). U = mg\,(h + d). Work Done Against Resistance:This energy is used to do work against the resistive force FavgF_{{avg}} over distance dd: W=Favg d.W = F_{{avg}}\,d. Equate Energy Loss to Work Done: mg (h+d)=Favg d⟹Favg=mg (h+d)d=mg(1+h/d).mg\,(h+d) = F_{{avg}}\,d F_{{avg}} = mg\,(h+d)/d = mg(1 + h/d). Thus, the average resistance offered by the wood is Favg=mg(1+h/d).{F_{{avg}} = mg(1 + h/d)}.

questions.question: Match the following
questions.explanation: (  A→Q,  B→P,  C→R)\;(\;A Q,\;B P,\;C R) A brief reasoning: (A) Work done by all forces equals the net work on the body, which by the Work–Energy Theorem is the change in kinetic energy (ΔK)( K). Thus, A→Q.A Q. (B) Work done by conservative forces is directly related to the change in potential energy (ΔU)( U), since Wconservative  =  − ΔU. W_{{conservative}} \;=\; -\, U. Thus, B→P.B P. (C) Work done by non‐conservative forces gives the change in the total mechanical energy (ΔEmech=Δ(K+U))( E_{{mech}} = (K+U)). Thus, C→R.C R.

questions.question: A force, F=2 t² , is applied on a block of mass m at rest as shown in the figure. Find the work done by the force in time t_o
questions.explanation: A convenient way to see this is via the Work–Energy Theorem. Since the block starts from rest on a frictionless surface, the net work done by the force from t=0t=0 to t=t0t=t_{0} equals the change in the block’s kinetic energy. Acceleration: F(t)  =  2 t²,a(t)  =  F(t)m  =  2 t²m.F(t)\;=\;2\,t², a(t)\;=\;F(t)/m\;=\;{2\,t²}{m}. Velocity: v(t)  =  ∫0ta(τ) dτ  =  ∫0t ⁣2 τ²m dτ  =  2/m [τ³3]0t  =  2 t³3 m.v(t)\;=\;_{0}^{t}a()\,d \;=\;_{0}^{t}\!{2\,²}{m}\,d \;=\;2/m\,[{³}{3}]_{0}^{t} \;=\;{2\,t³}{3\,m}. Final velocity at t=t0t=t_{0} is  v(t0)=2 t033 m\,v(t_{0})={2\,t_{0}³}{3\,m}. Change in Kinetic Energy (and hence the work done): W  =  ΔK  =  12 m [v(t0)]2  =  12 m (2 t033 m)2  =  2 t069 m.W \;=\; K \;=\;12\,m\,[v(t_{0})]² \;=\;12\,m\,({2\,t_{0}³}{3\,m})² \;=\;{2\,t_{0}⁶}{9\,m}.

questions.question: A block weighing 10 {~N} travels down a smooth curved track A B joined to a rough horizontal surface (figure). The rough surface has a friction coefficient of 0.20 with the block. If the block starts slipping on the track from a point 1.0 {~m} above the horizontal surface, the distance it will move on the rough surface is:

questions.question: The work done against gravity in taking 10 {~kg} . mass at 1 {~m} height in 1 {~s} will be
questions.explanation: The work done against gravity equals the increase in gravitational potential energy, given by: W=m g h.W = m\,g\,h. Substituting m=10 kgm = 10\,{kg}, g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\,{m/s}², and h=1 mh = 1\,{m}, we get W=10×9.8×1=98 J.W = 10 9.8 1 = 98\,{J}. The time of 1 s is irrelevant for calculating the work done. Thus, the work done is 98 J.

hi.question: गुरुत्व के विरुद्ध 10 kg द्रव्यमान को 1s में 1m की ऊँचाई पर ले जाने में किया गया कार्य होगा:
hi.explanation: गुरुत्व के विरुद्ध किया गया कार्य गुरुत्वीय स्थितिज ऊर्जा में वृद्धि के बराबर होता है, जो इस प्रकार दिया जाता है:: W=m g h.W = m\,g\,h. मानों m=10 kgm = 10\,{kg}, g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\,{m/s}², और h=1 mh = 1\,{m}, को प्रतिस्थापित करने पर, हमें प्राप्त होता है: W=10×9.8×1=98 J.W = 10 9.8 1 = 98\,{J}. कार्य की गणना करने के लिए 1 s का समय अप्रासंगिक है।. इस प्रकार, किया गया कार्य 98 J. है।

questions.question: A chain of mass m and length is placed on a table with one-sixth of it hanging freely from the table edge. The amount of work done to pull the chain on the table is
questions.explanation: Hanging Portion:16{1}{6} of the chain’s length (ℓ) is hanging off the table, so its mass is m6{m}{6}. Center of Mass of Hanging Part:The center of mass of that hanging segment is ℓ12{}{12} below the table surface. Initial Potential Energy (with table as zero level): Pi=(m6) g (−ℓ12)=− m g ℓ72.P_i = ({m}{6})\,g\,(-{}{12}) = -\,{m\,g\,}{72}. Final Potential Energy (once pulled up):The entire chain is on the table, so that segment’s potential energy is 00. Work Required:The work done equals the increase in potential energy: W=Pfinal−Pinitial=0−(− m g ℓ72)=m g ℓ72.W = P_{{final}} - P_{{initial}} = 0 - (-\,{m\,g\,}{72}) = {m\,g\,}{72}. Hence, the work needed to pull the chain fully onto the table is m g ℓ72{m\,g\,}{72}.

questions.question: A uniform chain of length L and mass M is lying on a smooth table and one third of its length is hanging vertically down over the edge of the table. If g is acceleration due to gravity, work required to pull the hanging part on to the table is
questions.explanation: Since the chain is uniform, the hanging portion (one‐third of the chain) has mass M3{M}{3}. That hanging segment’s center of mass is at the midpoint of its length L3{L}{3}, i.e.\ L6{L}{6} below the table. Taking the table level as the reference of zero potential energy: Initial potential energy of the hanging part: Ui  =  (M3)g (−L6)  =  − M g L18 . U_i \;=\;({M}{3}) g\,(-{L}{6}) \;=\;-\,{M\,g\,L}{18}\,. (The negative sign appears because the center of mass is L6{L}{6} below the reference.) Final potential energy (once the hanging part is pulled onto the table) is zero, since the entire chain is at the table level. Hence, the work required to pull the chain onto the table equals the increase in gravitational potential energy: W  =  Uf  −  Ui  =  0−(− M g L18)=  M g L18 .W \;=\;U_f \;-\;U_i \;=\;0 - (-\,{M\,g\,L}{18}) =\;{M\,g\,L}{18}\,.

questions.question: The work done in joules in increasing the extension of a spring of stiffness 10 {~N} / {cm} from 4 {~cm} to 6 {~cm} is

questions.question: Two springs A and B(k_{A}=2 k B) are stretched by applying forces of equal magnitudes at the four ends. If the energy stored in A is E , that in {B} is
questions.explanation: When a spring of stiffness kk is stretched by a force FF, its extension is x=F/kx = {F}{k}. The elastic potential energy is U=12 k x²=F²2 k.U = 12\,k\,x² = F²/2\,k. Given that kA=2 kBk_A = 2\,k_B and each spring is stretched by the same force FF: Energy in spring A: UA=F²2 kA=F²2 (2 kB)=F²4 kB.U_A = F²/2\,k_A = F²/2\,(2\,k_B) = F²/4\,k_B. Energy in spring B: UB=F²2 kB.U_B = F²/2\,k_B. Hence, UBUA=F²2 kBF²4 kB=42=2.U_B/U_A = {F²/2\,k_B}{F²/4\,k_B} = 4/2 = 2. Thus, if UA=EU_A = E, then UB=2EU_B = 2E.

hi.question: दो स्प्रिंग A और B के लिए kA=2kBk_A = 2k_B​ है। दोनों स्प्रिंगों के सिरों पर समान परिमाण का बल लगाकर उन्हें खींचा जाता है। यदि स्प्रिंग A में संचित ऊर्जा EE है, तो स्प्रिंग B में संचित ऊर्जा कितनी होगी?
hi.explanation: दिया है: kA=2kBk_A = 2k_B​ दोनों स्प्रिंगों पर समान बल FF लगाया गया है। स्प्रिंग A में संचित ऊर्जा EE है। स्प्रिंग में संचित ऊर्जा: U=F²2kU=F²/2k​ अर्थात, समान बल के लिए ऊर्जा स्प्रिंग नियतांक kkk के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है। U∝1/kU 1/k​ अब, kA=2kBk_A=2k_B​ तो, UBUA=kAkB=2U_B/U_A=k_A/k_B=2 चूँकि UA=EU_A=E UB=2EU_B=2E

questions.question: In stretching a spring by 2 {~cm} energy stored is given by {U} , then stretching by 10 {~cm} energy stored will be:

questions.question: Two springs of spring constant 3000 {~N} / {m} and 5000 {~N} / {m} respectively are streched with the same force. They will have potential energy in the ratio.

The stored energy in each spring is U=12kx²U = 12 kx². So U1=12 k1 (Fk1)2=F²2 k1,U2=12 k2 (Fk2)2=F²2 k2.U_1 = 12\,k_1\,({F}{k_1})² = {F²{2\,k_1}, U_2 = 12\,k_2\,({F}{k_2})² = {F²{2\,k_2}. Their ratio is U1U2=F²2 k1F²2 k2=k2k1=50003000=53.U_1/U_2 = {F²/2\,k_1}{{F²{2\,k_2}} = k_2/k_1 = 5000/3000 = 5/3. Hence, the ratio of their potential energies is 5:3.{5:3}.

questions.question: In a vertical circle of radius (r), at what point in its path a particle may have tension equal to zero:-
options: At a point horizontal from the centre of radius
questions.explanation: At the top of the vertical circle, the forces toward the center are gravity mgmg and the tension TT. The net centripetal force is T+mg=mv²r.T + mg = mv²/r. For the minimum speed at the top (just maintaining circular motion), v²=grv² = gr, making T+mg=mg,T + mg = mg, thus T=0T=0. Hence, the tension in the string can be zero at the highest point.

questions.question: A body crosses the topmost point of a vertical circle with critical speed. What will be its centripetal acceleration when the string is horizontal:
questions.explanation: At the top, the critical speed is vtop=grv_{{top}}=√(gr). When descending from the top to the horizontal position, the body falls by a vertical distance rr. Using energy conservation, the speed at the horizontal point is given by: vhor2=vtop2+2gr=gr+2gr=3gr.v_{{hor}}² = v_{{top}}² + 2gr = gr + 2gr = 3gr. Thus, the centripetal acceleration at the horizontal position is: ac=vhor2r=3grr=3g.a_c = {v_{{hor}}²{r} = 3gr/r = 3g.

questions.question: A body initially at rest and sliding along a frictionless track from a height {h} (as shown in the figure) just completes a vertical circle of diameter {AB}={D} . The height {h} is equal to:
questions.explanation: For the body just to complete the vertical circle of diameter DD, at the top of the circle the tension goes to zero, and gravity alone provides centripetal force: mg=mv²R,where R=D2.mg = m v²/R, {where }R = D/2. Hence, v²=g D2.v² = g \,{D}{2}. Let the body start from rest at height hh above the circle’s lowest point AA. The top of the circle is height DD above AA. By energy conservation: m g (h−D)=12 m v²    ⟹    g (h−D)=12 g D2    ⟹    h−D=D4    ⟹    h=5D4.m\,g\,(h - D) =12\,m\,v² \;\;\;\; g\,(h - D) =12\,g\,{D}{2} \;\;\;\; h - D = {D}{4} \;\;\;\; h = {5D}{4}.

questions.question: A cube of mass M starts at rest from point 1 at a height 4 {R} , where {R} is the radius of the circular track. The cube slides down the frictionless track and around the loop. The force which the track exerts on the cube at point 2 is
options: Cube will not reach the point 2
questions.explanation: Energy Conservation to Get Speed at Top:The cube is released from height 4R4R and reaches the top of the loop at height 2R2R.The drop in height is 4R−2R=2R4R - 2R = 2R.Thus, the gain in kinetic energy is: M g (2R)=12 M v².M\,g\,(2R) = 12\,M\,v². Solving gives: v²=4 g R.v² = 4\,g\,R. Centripetal Force at the Top:At the top of the loop, the net force required for circular motion is: Fcentripetal=M v²R=M (4 g R)R=4 M g.F_{{centripetal}} = M\,v²/R = M\,(4\,g\,R)/R = 4\,M\,g. Forces at the Top:Both gravity and the normal force act downward (toward the center) at the top. Therefore: N+M g=4 M g.N + M\,g = 4\,M\,g. Solving for the normal force: N=4 M g−M g=3 M g.N = 4\,M\,g - M\,g = 3\,M\,g. Thus, the force exerted by the track on the cube at the top is 3 M g3\,M\,g.
